title: Balochistan Home Minister Escapes Convoy Attack in Mastung on Pakistan's Independence Day
excerpt: Mir Ziaullah Langau was unharmed after gunmen opened fire on his security convoy traveling from Kalat to Quetta, wounding six security personnel in the latest escalation of violence in the restive province.
body:
• Balochistan Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langau escaped unhurt after armed assailants targeted his security convoy in Mastung district on Pakistan's Independence Day, August 14.
  • Six security personnel were wounded in the exchange of fire and were shifted to Nawab Ghous Bakhsh Hospital in Quetta for treatment.
  • The attack came three weeks after a sessions judge and his gunman were killed in a similar ambush in Mastung, and amid a broader surge in militant violence across the province.
  • Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa together account for 96% of all violence-related fatalities in Pakistan, according to a recent security report.

Balochistan's top security official narrowly escaped an armed attack on Pakistan's Independence Day when gunmen opened fire on his security convoy in the volatile Mastung district, officials confirmed on Thursday.

Home Minister Mir Ziaullah Langau's convoy was targeted while traveling from Kalat to Quetta. The Mastung additional deputy commissioner confirmed the attack, while police said Langau himself remained safe. At least six personnel from his security squad were wounded in the exchange of fire and were transported to Nawab Ghous Bakhsh Hospital in Quetta for treatment.

Defiant Response

Speaking after the attack, Langau struck a defiant tone. "I cannot be frightened by these firecrackers," the home minister said in Quetta, vowing that the attack would not weaken the government's resolve against militant groups operating in the province.

"I cannot be frightened by these firecrackers."

— Mir Ziaullah Langau, Balochistan Home Minister

No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack, though Mastung district has been a recurring flashpoint for separatist and militant violence in recent years.

Escalating Violence in Balochistan

The attack on Langau's convoy came just three weeks after a sessions judge and his gunman were killed when unidentified assailants opened fire on their vehicle in the same district. Additional Sessions Judge Tariq Lashari and another person were critically injured in that July 23 attack.

Violence in the province has intensified significantly in recent months. The Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), the province's most active militant separatist group designated as a terrorist organization by the United States, has claimed responsibility for multiple large-scale attacks on military convoys and government installations across the province.

In late July, the BLA claimed responsibility for an attack on a military convoy in Mastung's Khadkucha area, asserting that over 45 security personnel were killed. Pakistani officials confirmed the convoy had been attacked but did not release casualty figures. A second military convoy was targeted in the same area the following day.

A Province Under Siege

According to a report by the Centre for Research and Security Studies (CRSS), Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa together accounted for nearly 96% of all violence-related fatalities in Pakistan during the second quarter of 2026. Balochistan alone recorded 265 deaths — 34% of the national total — across 94 violent incidents during the quarter.

Pakistan has witnessed a surge in terror activities, particularly in its western provinces, since the Afghan Taliban came to power in 2021. Baloch separatist groups have long demanded independence from the central government, citing grievances over the exploitation of the province's gas and mineral resources and alleged enforced disappearances of activists.

The targeting of the home minister — the official directly responsible for the province's security apparatus — on Pakistan's Independence Day carries symbolic weight. It comes at a time when Islamabad faces mounting pressure to address the insurgency through both military operations and political engagement.

India-Pakistan Dimension

Pakistani officials have repeatedly accused India of supporting Baloch militant groups, a charge India has consistently denied. In recent statements, Pakistan's military has described killed militants as "India-backed terrorists," while India's foreign ministry has called such allegations "baseless" and "nothing but Pakistan's usual tactics to deflect attention from its own internal failings."

The ongoing violence in Balochistan remains closely watched in India, where the Baloch independence movement has periodically surfaced in diplomatic exchanges between the two nuclear-armed neighbors.
